extracted.intended_audience: authors, copyeditors, manuscript editors, and book/journal production staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, formatting, editing, and producing manuscripts for publication, including electronic workflow, markup, citations, illustrations, mathematical material, and responsibilities in multiauthor/multivolume works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript editing — basics
rubrics_metrics.description: Basics: author availability; author queries; author’s review; stages of editing; substantive vs. mechanical editing; style sheets; volume editor’s responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes author availability (2.52), author queries (see author queries), author’s review (2.2, 2.70–72, 2.82, 2.88, 2.101), stages of editing (2.53, 2.79), style sheets (2.55, 2.83, 2.111, fig. 2.3), substantive editing (2.48, 2.50, 2.51), mechanical editing (1.116, 2.45, 2.49), and volume editor responsibilities (2.41–42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking consistency and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-checking and consistency tasks for edited manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-checking (2.32–35, 2.53, 2.59); checking en dash use, note citations against reference lists and bibliographies, notes vs. reference numbers in text, style-sheet application, subhead hierarchy, and text citations against reference lists (2.14; 2.32; 2.62–63; 15.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic editing mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices and tools for editing in electronic files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backup copies (2.40, 2.78, 2.80); cleaning up files and removing embedded/hidden comments (2.39, 2.53, 2.59, 2.61, 2.79–80, 2.85, 14.5); document-comparison software (2.86); markup and word-processing styles (2.82–83, fig. 2.4); version control (2.5, 2.78–79); silent changes cautioned against (2.69, 2.85).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent professionals for manuscript editing
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use and what to expect from independent editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References independent professionals for editing (2.48, 2.73); covers author queries, discretion and flexibility, software knowledge, communications with authors, and production-process role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper-only manuscript editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions and mechanics when editing on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover circling, insertions/deletions/substitutions (2.92–95), marking conventions (2.91–99), backup copies (2.6, 2.71, 2.90), capitalizing/lowercasing marks (2.97), note renumbering (2.62), and interaction with proofreading (2.110).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing final manuscript for production
rubrics_metrics.description: Final checks and production preparation before typesetting or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking markup (2.73); checklist for final preparation (2.77); document-comparison use (2.86); pagination and running heads (2.75–76); type specifications (2.74); preparing running heads (2.76); and final check routines (2.89).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript editing — electronic-file cleanup and global changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Cleaning and making global edits in electronic files safely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global changes and when to apply them (2.69, 2.79, 2.80, 2.85); removing source-citation coding (14.5); using document comparison tools (2.86); careful handling to avoid silent changes (2.69, 2.85).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript editors — communications and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial communication practices and role in production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications with authors, checking author changes, cover letters and instructions, early contact and schedule (2.68–72); discretion and flexibility (2.48, 2.51, 2.64); post-proofreading tasks and production-process role (2.101, 2.2); software knowledge (2.79).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation guidelines for authors — basics
rubrics_metrics.description: Author-facing instructions for preparing submissions for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and consistency (2.7, 2.56, 13.6); checklist for submission (2.3); submission requirements and format (2.2, 2.3–6); letter to publisher and list of special characters (2.4, 2.3); proofreading before submission (2.100); publication process and schedule (2.2, figs. 2.1–2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation — cross-checking tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific cross-checks authors and editors should perform before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist of cross-checking tasks (2.32); citation data and format checking (14.5); cross-references (2.32, 2.35); verifying quotations (2.32, 2.33, 13.6); checking URLs (2.3, 2.32, 2.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation — electronic files
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and best practices for electronic manuscript files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and consistency of electronic files (2.7); backups and naming (2.4, 2.37, 2.40, 14.5); removing embedded/hidden comments (2.39); separate vs. single files (2.36, 2.80); removing source-citation coding (14.5); version control (1.112, 2.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirements for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting elements authors must follow when preparing manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting topics include abstracts and keywords (2.3, 2.25); bibliographies and reference lists (2.24, 14.67, 15.17); block quotations (2.11, 2.19–20, 13.9); chapter and part titles (2.17); dashes and hyphens (2.14, 2.13); italics and boldface (2.15, 12.63, 12.65); justification and margins (2.10); line spacing (2.6, 2.8, 2.19–20, 2.22–24); lists and numbering; notes (2.22, 14.24, 14.41, 14.43, 14.53); paragraphs and subheads (2.12, 2.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and tables — preparation and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for artwork, captions, numbering, file submission, and checks for illustrations and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artwork scans and inventory (2.27, 3.16–18); captions and identification (2.3, 2.26, 2.37); numbering of illustrations and tables (2.28, 2.29); preparation of tables (3.47); separate files for components (2.26, 2.36); submission guidelines and text callouts (3.3–4, 3.15; 2.26, 2.30, 2.32, 2.65–66); checking and adjusting tables (2.32, 3.81–88); handling continued lines and repeated column heads (3.86–87).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific parts of manuscript to check
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts that require particular editorial attention during manuscript preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions (2.65); cross-references (2.60); front matter (2.57); illustrations (2.65); indexes (2.67, 16.132–34); lists and outlines (2.21); mathematical copy (12.61–68); quotations and previously published material (2.61, 2.69, 2.91); source citations (2.62–64); subheads (2.59); tables (see tables guidance); titles of parts, chapters, and articles (2.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscripts — submission and version practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling submissions, versions, and post-submission changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviation for manuscripts (7.15, 7.33, 10.42, 14.226); acceptance procedures (4.52); file conversion (2.7, 2.79–80); length considerations (2.4, 2.52); making changes after submission (2.5); numbering pages (2.38); paper-only vs. electronic workflows (2.6, 2.8, 2.36–40); version of record (2.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Markup for manuscript editing (generic markup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of generic markup conventions for editing and production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview of generic markup (2.73); angle brackets, callouts, character-level formatting (2.16, 2.30, 2.81); tags for subheads and parts (2.81); tables and type specifications in markup (3.86; 2.74, 2.93); semantic markup (2.82n1, 7.49); differences vs. formal markup languages (2.81); integration into production checklists (2.77); interaction with paper-only markup (2.99).

rubrics_metrics.name: Markup languages, formal
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and concerns for formal markup languages in publishing workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to HTML, JATS, LaTeX, MathML, SGML, XHTML, XSL; accessibility issues; interaction with punctuation; metadata and Unicode requirements; semantic markup; word-processing styles; and use in electronic workflow and publishing (1.77, 1.117–119; 2.83; 11.2; 12.2; p. 981–990).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical copy — preparation and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for mathematical text, notation, fonts, and manuscript preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations in mathematical expressions (12.3, 12.11, 12.17, 12.64); enunciations (12.25, 12.56); fractions (12.45–49); manuscript preparation for math (12.61–68); fonts and kerning (12.11–13, 12.66); typefaces and subscripts/superscripts (12.63–68); potentially ambiguous symbols and resources (12.68, table 12.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical expressions — display and spacing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format, delimit, and space mathematical expressions in text and display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delimiters and common delimiters (12.26–35); display vs. inline (12.21–23); centering and numbering (12.21–25, 12.56); line breaks and reflow (12.23, 12.50); fractions and radicals (12.43–49); spacing rules (12.16–17, 12.19, 12.21–22); punctuation interaction with sentences (12.7, 12.18); summations, integrals, matrices, probability, statistics (12.39–42, 12.50–60).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line spacing and line breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on spacing for manuscripts and handling of line breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line spacing for manuscript editing and submission (2.6, 2.8, 2.19–20, 2.22–24); use in block quotations and between paragraphs/stanzas (13.22, 13.24, 13.25); line breaks with dashes and nonbreaking spaces (6.90, 6.82; 6.11; 6.119–121); widows and orphans (2.116–117).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists and outlines in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Formats, punctuation, and use of run-in vs vertical lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists in text: elided elements in math, outlines (2.21, 2.36, 6.127, 6.132), run-in lists and vertical lists formatting (6.128–132, 7.45); punctuation and placement rules; when to use lists vs tables (3.51); lists of abbreviations and lists of illustrations handling (1.39, 2.23, 14.60; 3.38–40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists of abbreviations and special characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating and formatting abbreviation lists and special-character inventories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alphabetizing abbreviation lists (1.44, fig. 1.8); cross-checking (2.32); format and placement (1.4, 1.44, 2.23, 14.60); lists of special characters (2.3, 2.16, 11.21, 11.122, 12.13); when to create abbreviation lists (10.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citations, locators, and bibliographic locators
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for locators in citations, page numbers, and alternative locators for electronic works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page numbers and other locators for bibliographies (14.65); locators in source citations: chapter numbers, folio editions, illustration/table numbers, line numbers, numbered notes, signed signatures (14.22; 14.53; 14.106–158); alternatives for electronic publications (1.123, 2.35, 14.22, 14.160, 14.174, 15.23); paragraph numbers as locators (1.125, 2.106, 14.148, 16.12–13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiauthor volumes — editorial and citation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for preparing and citing chapters and components in multiauthor collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors’ names handling (1.38, 1.50, 1.64, 2.32); consistent style across contributors (2.49); editor’s responsibilities (2.41–42); components to manage (appendixes, bibliographies, biographical notes, dedications, illustrations, notes, prefaces, table of contents); source-citation approaches for chapters (14.23, 15.9, 14.62, 15.10); indexing responsibilities and version control (2.42, 16.115).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multivolume works — components and citation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat multivolume works in production and citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Components like acknowledgments, indexes, pagination, titles and volume numbers; consistent style across volumes (2.49); source-citation standards for authors/editors, chapters, particular volume citations, volume and page numbers, and relationship to series (14.116–125; 15.41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia content — submission, metadata, and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for multimedia files, metadata, formats, and citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations for media terms (10.49); animations and video as supplemental content (1.107, 1.114, 14.187); archival practices (1.114); file formats and device specifications (2.4, 14.187, 14.261–68); metadata and DOIs for multimedia (1.75, 1.92); citation elements for recordings, performances, apps, audio/video, and online media (14.261–68, 15.57); handling still images and captions (3.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript production checklist items
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist elements to verify before sending manuscript to production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes checking markup and tags (2.73–77), backup copies, document comparison, pagination/running heads, type specifications, lists of special characters, separate files for components, and final content checks (2.77, 2.86, 2.74–76).
